name: Mango
description: Grow your audience and send newsletters with reviewed content and delivery reporting.
scope: One self-hosted newsletter and its equal operators. Mail is required; commerce, SMS, AI and email design are optional. Wider commerce and multichannel contract clauses remain release obligations.

capabilities.description: Base's Lobby at an installed Mango's `/` (Finish setup until the sender identity is saved, then Sign in) with `GET /setup/state`, and the static, hand-illustrated landing page at the run site's `/` (run-mango.com, Run Mango to `/run`) for the newsletter profile: Mango's mark and name, a hero, how a letter leaves Mango, consent, approval of the exact letter, scheduling, delivery reports, ownership and a closing call to action, linking to the Run page and the first-party docs, with the owner's configured name, one-line description and optional credit in the footer. It reads no record or session, sets no cookie, and loads only same-origin fonts, styles, scripts and favicons.

First-party public documentation at `/docs` for the people who run Mango: the repository Markdown that `docs/site.json` publishes, rendered to HTML at build time by a Vite plugin and served per request inside the public landing's shared header and footer, cookie-free and same-origin, describing the default newsletter profile only.

Base sessions and confirmed invitations, equal product powers, retained attribution, initial self-removal and last-active-operator protection; Local hosted acceptance proved mailed sign-in and native-session access on one disposable workers.dev installation, with no production authentication claim.
Imports customers, products, orders, refunds, carts, and browsing events from one connected commerce store, tracks per-source freshness, and blocks approval on stale or missing sources.
Tracks each contact's independent per-channel consent state, evidence, opt-outs, imports, merges, dormancy, and erasure with a surviving opt-out record.
Generates ranked, evidence-cited campaign proposals from store data with grounded AI content and honest forecast provenance, held as drafts until an operator approves a revision.
Resolves and rechecks campaign audiences against consent, commerce, dormancy, and frequency rules, freezing the candidate set at approval and re-excluding at dispatch.

Operator-authored blank and recorded-signal drafts without AI, shared proposal Review, rich/HTML content with managed footer and plain text, structured live audience counts, store-zone scheduling, exact-revision approval and pause/resume, cancellation and test-send controls.

Signed-in operators upload JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP campaign images, checked by their own header bytes, size and pixel dimensions. Each is stored once in R2 under its SHA-256, never changed or deleted except by contact erasure of bytes holding an erased identifier, and served publicly at `/media/<sha256>` with an immutable cache, its exact content type, no cookie and no session, rate-limited per image rather than per client address, recording nothing about who fetched it. Approval verifies these images in storage instead of fetching the deployment's own hostname.

An operator imports a design made with their own 12ui CLI (a LayerDoc version 2 file and its PNG candidate) into a draft's email body. The browser crops the photos and stores them as campaign images, compiles a 600px table email in the validated email grammar with the operator's HTTPS button link and Mango's managed footer, and highlights every line not in the operator's brief. Import only makes an unsaved edit and itself makes no request to 12ui.

With the optional design module configured (the owner's own 12ui API key and origin), an operator editing a draft can ask for designs from a brief prefilled from the draft. A background run on the owner's 12ui account draws two to four candidates, shown as they land and kept across reloads; the operator picks one with Use this design, Mango fetches its layout as a LayerDoc and the browser then builds the email through the design import path, keeping the run on offer until the draft is saved with it. Estimates come before each paid step, each paid request records a cost fact, a rate-limit wait and every failure are shown with Mango's own reason, every request to 12ui has a time limit, and nothing is saved, approved, scheduled or sent by the run. With the module off, nothing is shown and 12ui is never contacted.
Enforces sender identity, authentication, unsubscribe and opt-out mechanics, link and content checks, personalisation fallbacks, and sending-reputation limits before any send.

Hands recipient-steps to email and SMS providers under their declared retry guarantees, reconciles unknown outcomes where evidence is available, throttles retry-safe transport failures, and pauses a channel during a provider outage; SendGrid uses at-most-once handoff and operator-reviewed uncertainty.

Reports campaign history, engagement, attribution, cost, tracked-link activity, and deliverability without presenting forecasts as facts. Optional privacy-sensitive open estimates require a persisted operator opt-in in Insights and are disabled by default. A signed first-party /o/:token pixel counts at most one image-load estimate per recipient-step, never reads or delivery, click, attribution or confidence evidence. Disabling revokes old tokens, and contact erasure removes recipient-specific tokens and facts.

Exports every contact, source record, consent record, campaign, and audit entry as JSON alongside uploaded campaign assets. Private export/restore data includes signup_settings (frequency disclosure and exact embed origins), open_tracking_settings (operator preference/audit, disabled by default, generation), open_tracking_tokens (signed token digest, recipient-step, generation and expiry) and open_estimate_facts (recipient-step and first occurrence only). Contact erasure removes linked open tokens/facts; no IP, user agent or cookie is stored for open estimates.

nonGoals: Store transactional messaging (order, shipping, and account notifications)

externals.why: Mango needs the buyer's real customers, products, carts, browsing signals, orders, refunds, and inventory to identify and recheck opportunities.
data: Webhook acknowledgements sent back to the store confirming receipt of an event
Explicit adapter requests for source records (customers, products, orders, refunds, carts, browsing events)

externals.why: A language model turns structured evidence into reviewable campaign content and explanations; Cloudflare primitives do not provide that model capability.
data: The proposal evidence required for the requested generation
The configured business context required for the requested generation

externals.why: An image-generation design service (12ui, reached with the owner's own API key) turns an operator's brief into candidate email designs and a structured layout; Cloudflare primitives do not generate designs. It is contacted only when an operator asks for designs or chooses one, never otherwise. Privacy: No contact, audience, personalisation value or token is sent. 12ui's sub-processors are OpenAI, fal.ai, Google and Cloudflare, and 12ui may keep briefs and images in its internal evaluation corpus until the account owner asks for deletion. 12ui's generated artifacts expire after 7 days, so Mango stores the candidates and layout it uses in its own R2 bucket.
data: The operator's design brief, prefilled from the draft's name, subject, preheader, sender name and current text and edited by the operator, with every {{...}} personalisation or managed token removed, inside Mango's fixed description of an email layout
The chosen candidate image, sent back for layout conversion
The owner's design-service API key, as bearer authentication

externals.why: Internet email delivery, domain authentication, bounce handling, and complaint feedback require a delivery provider with established sending infrastructure. Managed hosting explicitly selects RER for transactional sign-in and subscription confirmations; Free and Assisted hosting retain their own-provider connections.
data: Approved email content
Sender metadata for direct providers; the RER relay chooses its own sending identity.
Each eligible recipient's email address
Operator email addresses that receive magic links, test sends, and dispatch-paused notices
Diagnostic sender-verification message and configured receipt mailbox; provider message IDs and sender-domain names for delivery reconciliation and authentication queries

With MAIL_PROVIDER=rer, only one recipient address, subject, text and optional HTML go to the RER-assigned HTTPS MAIL_RELAY_URL, authenticated by the server-only MAIL_API_KEY. Active Managed access and a valid credential are required.

externals.why: Registered sending numbers, carrier routing, country approval, compliance keywords, and delivery receipts require a telecommunications provider.
data: Approved SMS content
Programme metadata
Each eligible recipient's phone number

externals.why: A public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver verifies that each approved external link, image and redirect target resolves outside private networks before dispatch. Images this deployment stores itself at /media/ are verified in its own storage and never resolved or fetched.
data: Approved link host names only

externals.why: Optional abuse prevention on hosted and embedded signup. Only a trusted pointer or keyboard interaction with the form loads the browser challenge. The server verifies the token before accepting consent.
data: After interaction, browser requests https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js and its challenge frames, disclosing the public site key, visitor IP and browser challenge signals to Cloudflare.

Server POST to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify sends the challenge token, visitor IP and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY; acceptance requires newsletter-signup action and the configured public hostname. No email address or consent evidence is sent to Cloudflare.
externals.requiredWhen: Both TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY (public browser configuration) and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (server-only secret) are configured; one-sided configuration is refused.

externals.why: Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS verifies sender domain authentication records before dispatch.
data: Sender domain and DKIM/SPF/DMARC record names queried at https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query; no recipients or message bodies.

externals.why: Dispatch preflight checks explicitly approved external links and images, including each allowed redirect, for reachability after DNS safety checks.
data: Full approved destination URLs including paths and query parameters sent as HEAD requests to configured allowed hosts. No operator cookie or provider credential is attached. Deployment-hosted /media/ images use local storage instead.

externals.why: An authenticated owner can open the configured Run Edit Run editor and explicitly share page context for requested visual edits.
data: The configured management origin receives installation identifier and application origin in the editor iframe URL after the owner opens it.

The origin-checked protocol sends page path, editor visibility and edit results. Only while context sharing is enabled, it additionally sends page title, bounded visible DOM text and selected element metadata (excluding input values and private-marked elements).
externals.requiredWhen: RER_MANAGEMENT_ORIGIN and RER_INSTALLATION_ID configure the optional authenticated owner editor.

externals.why: An installer-selected authenticated receipt service supplies original diagnostic email and trusted authentication observations before marketing sending is enabled. The optional paired MAILBOX_RECEIPT_URL and MAILBOX_RECEIPT_RECIPIENT inputs select its HTTPS origin, secret URL token and diagnostic mailbox; redirects and off-origin responses are refused.
data: Authenticated GET requests carry the server-only receipt URL token, diagnostic recipient address, challenge nonce and sent-at timestamp to find the diagnostic email.
The matching receipt ID is sent to the same origin to retrieve original diagnostic message bytes; no audience contacts or campaign content are sent by this lookup.
externals.requiredWhen: The authenticated sender receipt connector is configured and an operator verifies a diagnostic challenge

operatingCost.assumptions: One store, 10000 contacts, 4 campaigns per month, 20000 email and 5000 SMS recipient-steps, and 500 AI generations. Queue messages are at most 64 KB and dispatch stays below 3334 recipient-steps per UTC day. Every campaign image fetched from an inbox is one Worker request and one D1 row write for its per-image rate counter; at 4 images per email, 20000 email recipient-steps add up to 80000 of each per month, concentrated on send days, and they count toward the same daily Free quotas as everything else. Each design run with the optional design module is one Worker request to start it, about 5 to 15 Queue messages while it polls (three operations each), one R2 write per candidate image and one for the layout, and a few D1 rows; 12ui itself bills the owner's own account at about $0.03 per candidate and $0.05 per layout at its 12 October 2026 list prices, free within its daily allowance of 20 images and 50 layouts.
operatingCost.cloudflareMonthlyUsd: $0 on the current Workers Free plan while the deployment stays inside every Free quota: at most 100000 dynamic Worker requests per UTC day with 10 ms CPU per invocation; 10000 Queue operations per UTC day (write, read, and delete are each one operation per 64 KB); D1 at 5 million rows read per UTC day, 100000 rows written per UTC day, and 5 GB total storage; and SQLite Durable Objects at 100000 requests and 13000 GB-s per UTC day. Workers Paid starts at $5/month and is required for the declared 100000-contact campaign: its 100000 recipient-step writes plus step and schedule mutations exceed D1 Free's 100000 rows-written-per-UTC-day limit.
operatingCost.externalMonthlyUsd: Not yet estimated because the reference commerce, email, SMS, and AI adapters have not been selected; required before first release.
